market.summary: A softer start looks likely after four strong days: GIFT Nifty is down about 0.2% and Asia is weak, with the Nikkei off about 3% on AI and tech worries. US futures also fell as early midterm returns favoured Democrats, though no final result is in. Crude easing and three days of foreign buying are the offsets. For open trades this is a possible dip at the open, not a change of plan; the NIFTY 500 is still under its 200 DMA, so the screener's size-down message stands.

points.text: GIFT Nifty 23,704.5, down 55.5 points (0.23%) at 8:36 IST. Nikkei -3.03%, KOSPI -1.49%. Dow and S&P 500 futures -0.72% and -1.07%, with Democrats leading in early results.
US close 3 Nov: Dow -0.38% to 51,786.72, S&P 500 +0.36% to 7,568.92, Nasdaq +0.83% to 25,372.01. Rupee about 94.73 per dollar; India VIX 15.72.
Early midterm count at about 8 pm ET favoured Democrats; only a part of the races had been called. Asian tech fell on worry that a Democratic sweep could slow AI investment.
AMD beat after the US close: revenue $13.38 bn (+45% YoY) vs $13.09 bn expected, adjusted EPS $2.09 vs $1.95; shares rose up to 9%, then about 4% after hours.
Brent January futures $103.20, down 1.07%. No new tariff or Trump trade item in the morning market reports read.
Provisional 3 Nov cash flows: FIIs bought Rs 6,836.81 Cr, DIIs sold Rs 3,678.85 Cr. NIFTY 500 22,520 vs 50 DMA 22,522 and 200 DMA 22,764; 30% of tracked stocks above their 21-day EMA.
